tools.name: search_changelogs
tools.description: Find a public LogPulse changelog by package name, repository, product name or slug. Returns slugs to use with the other tools.

tools.name: get_changelog
tools.description: Get a changelog's name, repository, packages, latest version and feed links.

tools.name: list_releases
tools.description: List published releases, newest first, with versions, breaking changes, migration steps and deprecations.

tools.name: get_release
tools.description: Get one release by version (2.0.0 or v2.0.0) or URL slug, with full notes, breaking changes and deprecations.

tools.name: compare_versions
tools.description: Answer “what changed between two versions, and what do I need to change?”: breaking changes with migration steps, deprecations and every release after `from` up to `to`.

tools.name: get_roadmap
tools.description: Get the public roadmap: items under review, planned, in progress and shipped, with vote counts.

tools.name: convert_changelog
tools.description: Turn any project's CHANGELOG.md text, or a GitHub release, releases page, repository or changelog file URL, into a machine-readable changelog: versions, dates, breaking changes with migration steps, and deprecations. Works for projects that aren't on LogPulse. Returns an llms.txt-style summary plus

tools.name: publish_release
tools.description: Publish a release note to your LogPulse changelog right after shipping — with version, breaking changes, migration steps and deprecations. Needs a LogPulse API key with the “Publish releases” permission, sent as the Authorization header.

tools.name: post_roadmap_update
tools.description: Add an item to your LogPulse roadmap, or update one by id — move it to in progress or shipped, change its ETA, or link the release that shipped it. Needs a LogPulse API key with the “Update roadmap” permission, sent as the Authorization header.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "publish_release" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_changelog, get_release, get_roadmap · Private data: convert_changelog, publish_release, post_roadmap_update · Public sink: publish_release, post_roadmap_update.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_changelog, get_release, get_roadmap · Private data: convert_changelog, publish_release, post_roadmap_update · Public sink: publish_release, post_roadmap_update

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
